day1_insight: There's been no rain at all lately, so there's no runoff driving contamination, and strong summer sunlight is helping disinfect the water. The model's main signals right now: high tide level is raising risk — a high tide can mobilize bacteria held in wet sand and push the waterline toward outfalls; hours since high tide is raising risk — the timing relative to high tide affects how concentrated bacteria are at the shoreline; and seasonal pattern is raising risk — seasonal patterns (wet winters vs dry summers) set the baseline risk. The most recent sample, 7 days ago, was excellent at 5 MPN/100mL. It's a naturally clean, well-flushed open-coast beach (unsafe only ~3% of the time), so outside of storms it's reliably safe.
